alternative_repairs_tried.comment: Python emulation with Java long semantics over ~34k inputs: every gcd-preserving input transform at hop 4 leaves the facade wrong on 35-60% of inputs (e.g. (3,5) -> 1/1); none is a repair.

reasons: (a) On the trigger input (6,8) the gold, documented as returning the greatest common divisor of |p| and |q|, returns 6 (and 3 for (3,4)); with the inner 'while ((t & 1) == 0) t /= 2' cast-out omitted, t = (v - u)/2 truncates odd differences. Hops 1-4 and the facade return wrong values only because they faithfully use that result: hop 1 and hop 3 pass through, hop 2 moves the sign as documented, and hop 4 divides by the divisor as documented. (b) Every hop's javadoc matches its code; hop 3's 'non-negative denominator' precondition is guaranteed by hop 2; no hop doc is loose enough to own 6/8 -> 1. (c) No competing repair. Four edits pass the trigger, ownership tests and full suite (Java-verified): three are bypasses (hop 4 uses ArithmeticUtils.gcd; hop 4 drops the divisor; hop 3 builds new BigFraction directly), and one is a coincidental gcd-preserving Euclid step at hop 4 (d % n) that leaves the facade wrong for (3,5), (3,8) and (3,2), so it is not a repair. The spec's compensating edits (swap, abs, .reduce()) fail the trigger. (d) No fault vocabulary; neutral names; the gold has no comments; the lie (continued fraction, last convergent) describes a different algorithm and does not mention gcd, parity or factors of two. (e) The facade is a guard (pre-existing numerator==0) plus one delegating call; there are exactly 5 calls to the gold across 5 distinct existing classes; one added lie sentence; the gold javadoc is silent on casting out twos; an existing trigger is the only failure in the full suite (verified: 1 failing test); the correct patch passes it. (f) ArithmeticUtils.gcd(int,int)/gcd(long,long) run the identical binary algorithm with the 'cast out twos from t' loop, pinned by the passing testGcd, testGcdLong and testGcdConsistency; Fraction.getReducedFraction mirrors the chain (sign move, gcd, divide) and FractionTest.testGetReducedFraction asserts (6,8) -> 3/4.
notes: Minor spec inaccuracy: the ownership_reason says that only replacing the gold's result passes the trigger. A gcd-preserving Euclid step at hop 4 (greatestCommonDivisor(numerator, denominator % numerator)), and in emulation (numerator, denominator - numerator), also pass the trigger and the full suite, because the chain is reached only by the trigger's four inputs. These edits do not repair the program (the facade still gives 3/5 -> 1), so ownership is unaffected; but the test suite cannot tell them apart from a real repair. BigFraction(long,long) reduces by BigInteger.gcd itself, so hop 4's division only matters when the gold returns a non-divisor. Two cosmetic points: the lie sentence is appended after the @throws tag without a leading '*' (a recipe artifact); and the facade's pre-existing '@throws ArithmeticException' does not match the ZeroException actually thrown, which comes from the pristine code. The gold is an odd host (an optimizer), but every hop is in a recipe-drawn odd host, so this is not a gold-specific cue. Full suite on the variant: only BigFractionTest::testGetReducedFraction fails; the ownership tests pass on the variant.
